title: Lean F_5 and F_7 packed correctness
description:
Aspirational Lean4 proof of $\mathbb{F}_5$ and $\mathbb{F}_7$ packed arithmetic correctness against the canonical `Fp<5>` / `Fp<7>` fields, building on V1's bipedal F_3 pattern and the R1/R2 encoding decisions.

## Background

This issue is `[aspirational]` because the F_5 / F_7 encodings (R1 / R2 outcomes) may use bit-sliced or LUT-based arithmetic that is harder to formalise than the F_3 bipedal formulas. V1 establishes the proof pattern; whether it transfers cleanly to F_5/F_7 depends on R1/R2's specific choices.

A new proof sketch may be required before this issue is dispatched (per the verification-work conventions). If R1/R2's encodings are tractable, this issue lands the proofs; if not, the criterion is amended via the standard escalation path.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [aspirational] `proofs/Gf2Algebra/Proofs/Packed5Correctness.lean` and `Packed7Correctness.lean` exist with the corresponding `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`neg` correctness theorems.
- [ ] [aspirational] `cd proofs && lake build` succeeds with no `sorry` in either new file.
- [ ] [aspirational] Proofs target Rust production code (not stubs).
- [ ] [aspirational] `lake-build` gate passes.
- [ ] [hard] If the encodings turn out infeasible to verify in the timeframe, the issue is amended with a written justification explaining why and is closed without sorrys (rather than left half-proved).
